what_worked: Revenue skew narrative is directionally correct and the arc from geography to takeaway has logical flow.
fix_next: Replace fabricated-looking charts with verifiable data; acknowledge missingness, cite actual category/provider/TLD findings from the dataset.
verdict: Surface-level story with multiple unverifiable charts and motivational filler masking thin analysis.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2: claims 'over 40%' US share without accounting for 241 missing country values (~24% of data). Slide 3: '22.86% total conversion rate' is unexplained and unverifiable; labels revenue as 'MRR' when dataset records 30-day revenue. Slide 4: growth-rate distribution (30/30/20/12/8) uses suspiciously round numbers with no corresponding variable in the reference data—appears fabricated. Slide 5: pie chart percentages (40/35/15/10) for followers-vs-revenue quadrants are unverifiable and sum too neatly. Slide 3: '60% of startups have yet to break even' is an unsupported claim with no cost data in the dataset.

evidence.insight: No analysis of categories, payment providers, TLDs, anonymity, or sale multiples. Observations ('most startups are small,' 'followers ≠ revenue') are generic truisms, not dataset-specific discoveries.
evidence.narrative: Loose geography→revenue→growth→social→takeaway arc exists but lacks a unifying thesis. Each slide reads as an independent observation rather than building toward a synthesized argument.
evidence.framing: Title frames dataset as '1,000 AI startups' when it spans 12+ categories beyond AI. No mention of data source, collection method, 241 missing countries, 274 missing categories, or 216 zero-revenue rows. Audience ('for you') is undefined.
evidence.accuracy: Slide 4 growth chart appears wholly invented—no growth-rate field exists in the reference data to produce those bins. Slide 5 pie chart percentages are unverifiable. Slide 3 conflates 30-day revenue with MRR and introduces an unexplained '22.86% conversion rate.' Slide 2 ignores massive country missingness. Slide 3 claims '60% haven't broken even' without cost data.
evidence.visual: Gamma template is clean and legible but repetitive dark-mesh background is purely decorative. Three-column takeaway cards repeat on every slide. Pie chart on slide 5 is a poor choice. Suspiciously round bar values on slide 4 undermine credibility.
evidence.ai_slop: Pervasive motivational filler: 'The AI era is just beginning,' 'Consistency beats virality,' 'Hype doesn't pay the bills,' 'one paying customer at a time.' Three-column insight cards on every slide are a generic AI template pattern. Content could describe any startup dataset.

change_reason: Preliminary scores are well-calibrated. Fabricated charts, unverifiable claims, absent dataset-specific analysis, and heavy AI filler all justify the low marks across dimensions. No adjustment needed.
